questions.prompt: Why can a 2 KB text file conceal a 5 MB executable?
options: A named stream's size does not count toward the file size Explorer reports
The executable is stored in the registry instead
questions.explanation: Named streams are invisible to ordinary listing and their size is excluded from the reported file size, so the host file appears unchanged.

questions.prompt: What forensic value does the Zone.Identifier stream provide?
options: It stores the file's SHA-256 hash
It carries Mark of the Web data including ZoneId and, on newer Windows, HostUrl and ReferrerUrl -- frequently proving where a file came from
It records every user who opened the file
It prevents the file from being deleted
questions.explanation: Because it survives renaming and moving, Zone.Identifier is a durable record of a file's origin -- and its absence on an externally-sourced file is itself informative.

questions.prompt: Why did attackers begin delivering malware inside ISO and VHD containers?
options: Those formats historically did not propagate Mark of the Web to the files inside, stripping the mark that causes Office to block macros
ISO files bypass all antivirus scanning
questions.explanation: MOTW-marked documents have macros blocked by Office, so a delivery path that strips the mark restores macro execution -- which drove a real shift in attacker tradecraft.

questions.prompt: Which Sysmon event provides proactive detection of ADS creation?
options: Event ID 15 (FileCreateStreamHash), which logs stream creation along with a hash
questions.explanation: Event ID 15 converts an artifact you would otherwise have to go hunting for with dir /R into an event that arrives on its own.
